summary: Inject critical warning into executor context when all tools in a step fail, forcing re-examination of original pixels.

edits.hypothesis: Injecting a high-priority user message when all tools in a step fail prevents the agent from uncritically accepting subsequent negative VQA outputs by explicitly directing it to re-examine original pixels.
edits.why_not_lower_lever: Prompt edits in toolset.py are static and do not react to dynamic runtime failures; this control-flow change activates only when the specific failure pattern (all tools failing) occurs, providing contextual guidance exactly when needed.
edits.trigger_condition: When every tool call in a single decision step returns a failure status (tool_failures_in_step == len(actions)).
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) In q000001, q000004, q000005, q000008, and q000009, the roi_crop tool failed. With this edit, the agent receives a CRITICAL warning before calling llava_med_qa, reducing the likelihood of accepting its negative finding without further scrutiny. (preservative) Success cases like q000003 and q000007 do not trigger this condition as they either skip tools or succeed, so their habits are preserved. (transfer) Generalizes to any task where targeted inspection tools fail, ensuring robustness against backend errors.
edits.regression_risk: Minimal; the warning is only injected on total step failure, which is rare in successful trajectories. It may increase token usage slightly but improves accuracy in failure modes.
edits.mechanism: Injecting a high-priority user message when all tools in a step fail prevents the agent from uncritically accepting subsequent negative VQA outputs by explicitly directing it to re-examine original pixels.
